'''Paul Victor Louis Zipser''' (born 18 February 1994) is a German professional [[basketball]] player for [[USC Heidelberg|MLP Academics Heidelberg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL). Standing at {{convert|2.03|m|ftin|abbr=on}}, he mainly plays at the [[small forward]] position. He was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] with the 48th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].

==Professional career==

===Heidelberg (2010–2012)===
Zipser began his professional career in his hometown with [[USC Heidelberg]] in 2010. In 2011–12, he averaged 7.9 points, 3 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paul Zipser Basketball Profile|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Paul_Zipser/Germany/BMuenchen/202754|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=25 April 2015}}</ref> He managed just two games for Heidelberg in 2012–13 due to injury.

=== Bayern Munich (2013–2016) ===
On 18 January 2013, Zipser signed a four-year deal with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/98452/bayern-munich-signs-paul-zipser-to-a-four-year-deal.html|title=Bayern Munich signs Paul Zipser to a four-year deal|work=Sportando.com|date=18 January 2013|access-date=18 July 2015}}</ref>

On 21 April 2015, Zipser entered the [[2015 NBA draft]] as an early-entrant,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/159052/paul-zipser-enters-the-2015-nba-draft.html|title=Paul Zipser enters the 2015 NBA Draft|work=Sportando.com|date=21 April 2015|access-date=25 April 2015}}</ref> only to withdraw from it later.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/163628/paul-zipser-withdraws-from-the-2015-nba-draft.html|title=Paul Zipser withdraws from the 2015 NBA Draft|work=Sportando.com|date=11 June 2015|access-date=18 July 2015}}</ref>

In 2015–16, Zipser played 40 league games for Bayern Munich, averaging 7.1 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 18.5 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/statistiken/spieler/portraits/p/16358-paul-zipser/|work=EasyCredit-BBL.de|title=Paul Zipser BBL 2015-2016 Stats|access-date=29 May 2016|language=de}}</ref> For the season, he was named the League's [[Basketball Bundesliga Best German Young Player|Best German Young Player]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/n/news/2016/5-mai/awards-herbert-und-zipser/|title=Auszeichnungen: Gordon Herbert ist "Trainer des Jahres" / Paul Zipser "Bester deutscher Nachwuchsspieler U22"|work=EasyCredit-BBL.de|date=11 May 2016|access-date=11 May 2016|language=de}}</ref>

In June 2016, Zipser attended the Adidas Eurocamp, a basketball camp based in Treviso for the NBA Draft prospects. He was named the Eurocamp 2016 [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.adidaseurocamp.com/eurocamp-2016-awards/|title=EUROCAMP 2016 Awards|work=AdidasEurocamp.com|access-date=13 June 2016|archive-date=9 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209195442/http://adidaseurocamp.com/eurocamp-2016-awards/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2016–2018)===
On 23 June 2016, Zipser was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] with the 48th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2016/story/_/id/16423806/2016-nba-draft-chicago-bulls-draft-paul-zipser-german-sf-no-48-overall|title=Chicago Bulls draft Paul Zipser, German SF, at No. 48 overall|work=ESPN.com|date=23 June 2016|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref> On 15 July, he signed with the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/release/bulls-sign-paul-zipser|title=BULLS SIGN PAUL ZIPSER|work=NBA.com|date=15 July 2016|access-date=15 July 2016}}</ref> On 12 January 2017, in just his 11th appearance of the season, Zipser made his first career start in the Bulls' 104–89 loss to the [[New York Knicks]]; he had a then season-high seven points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400900008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170114123428/http://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400900008|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 January 2017|title=Knicks beat Bulls with big games from Anthony, Rose, Noah|work=ESPN.com|date=12 January 2017|access-date=13 January 2017}}</ref> On 22 March, he scored a career-high 15 points in a 117–95 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900456|title=Mirotic scores season-high 28, Bulls beat Pistons 117-95|work=ESPN.com|date=22 March 2017|access-date=23 March 2017}}</ref> In the Bulls' regular-season finale on 12 April, Zipser set a new career high with 21 points in a 112–73 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to the [[Windy City Bulls]], Chicago's [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=17 December 2016|archive-date=26 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Throughout 2017–18 season, he received very little playing time due to the Bulls' front office trying to develop other young talents. He was sent down to their G-League affiliate, the Windy City Bulls on several occasions. Zipser began seeing more playing time during the middle of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900600|title=Bulls clinch playoff spot with 112-73 rout over Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=12 April 2017|access-date=13 April 2017}}</ref> On 18 May 2018, Zipser was reported to have surgery in repairing a broken left foot.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bulls F Paul Zipser has surgery to repair broken left foot|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/05/18/chicago-bulls-f-paul-zipser-has-surgery-repair-broken-left-foot|website=NBA.com |access-date=18 May 2018 |date=18 May 2018}}</ref> On 14 July, he was waived by the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web |title=BULLS SIGN JABARI PARKER |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-jabari-parker |website=NBA.com |access-date=15 July 2018 |date=14 July 2018}}</ref>

===San Pablo Burgos (2019)===
After being close to signing with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] according to media reports in January 2019, Zipser moved to Spanish [[Liga ACB]] side [[CB Miraflores|San Pablo Burgos]] on 17 January 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=145265 |title=ACB.COM - Paul Zipser se suma al proyecto del San Pablo Burgos |access-date=18 January 2019 |archive-date=17 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190117220343/http://acb.com/redaccion.php?id=145265 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Return to Bayern Munich (2019–2023) ===
On 5 August 2019 Zipser signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fcbayern.com/basketball/de/news/2019-20/08/zipser-2021|title=Paul Zipser kehrt zu den Bayern zurück|last=|first=|date=August 5, 2019|website=fcbayern.com|publisher=|language=de|access-date=March 7, 2022}}</ref>

=== Return to Heidelberg (2023–present) ===
On 1 July 2023, after a break of 11 years, he signed for a second stint with [[MLP Academics Heidelberg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlp-academics-heidelberg.de/paukenschlag-die-rueckkehr-von-paul-zipser-zu-den-mlp-academics-ist-perfekt-39644|title=tDie Rückkehr von Paul Zipser zu den MLP Academics ist perfek|last=|first=|date=July 11, 2023|website=mlp-academics-heidelberg.de|publisher=|language=de|access-date=July 12, 2023}}</ref>

==National team career==
Zipser has been a member of the German national [[Germany national under-17 basketball team|under-16]] and [[Germany national basketball team|under-18]] teams. He played in the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|2011]] and [[2012 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. In [[2012 Albert Schweitzer Tournament|2012]] he also played in [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]] and was named to the All-Tournament Team, averaging 14.6 points, 5 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_WI0u,B3DGtkbYppl6GwCd1.coid_eCotC1BYHTgvawrLw3FuR2.articleMode_on.html|title=SPAIN WINS ALBERT SCHWEITZER TOURNAMENT|work=FIBAEurope.com|date=16 April 2012|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Paul-Zipser/Summary/26506|title=Paul Zipser Player Profile|work=RealGM.com|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref>

On 30 July 2015, Zipser made his debut for the [[Germany national basketball team]] in a game against [[Austria national basketball team|Austria]]. During [[EuroBasket 2015|FIBA EuroBasket 2015]], he averaged 5.2 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_288.playerID_83490.html|title=Paul Zipser|work=EuroBasket2015.org|access-date=8 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220124206/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_288.playerID_83490.html|archive-date=20 December 2016|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

==Personal life==
During [[EuroBasket 2015]], Zipser raised controversy by refusing to sign an autograph for Vuk Ivanović, a boy of Serbian descent who was wearing a Serbian jersey, who claimed he wants to sell the autograph later.<ref name="autograph">{{cite web|title=German basketball player refuses to sign a boy's autograph because he is a Serb|url=http://www.telegraf.rs/english/1741413-scandal-at-eurobasket-german-basketball-player-refuses-to-sign-a-boys-autograph-because-he-is-a-serb-exclusive-video|website=telegraf.rs|access-date=12 April 2017|date=9 September 2015}}</ref> However, Zipser gave an autographed game-worn jersey and shorts to [[Saint Sava Serbian Orthodox Church (Merrillville, Indiana)|Saint Sava Serbian Orthodox Church]] for a special raffle at 2018 SerbFest in [[Merrillville, Indiana]].<ref>{{cite web|title=SerbFest – Saint Sava Serbian Orthodox Church – Merrillville, Indiana|url=http://www.saintsava.net/serbfest/|quote=Nikola Mirotic and Paul Zipser 2016 - 2017 Season Chicago Bulls Game-Worn Autographed Jersey and Shorts}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=January 2019}}
